q: A railway servant retires on superannuation after rendering 21 years of qualifying service, that is, 42 completed six-monthly periods. His emoluments at retirement are Rs 68,000 per month. The retirement gratuity payable to him, at one-fourth of a month's emoluments for each completed six-monthly period of qualifying service, will be:
e: Retirement gratuity is one-fourth of a month's emoluments for each completed six-monthly period. So 42 periods x (Rs 68,000 / 4) = 42 x Rs 17,000 = Rs 7,14,000.

q: A railway servant retires on superannuation with 210 days of Leave on Average Pay at his credit. His pay plus Dearness Allowance at retirement is Rs 78,000 per month. The cash equivalent of leave salary payable to him, computed at one-thirtieth of the monthly amount for each day of leave at his credit, will be:
e: Cash equivalent of leave salary is (pay plus DA) / 30 per day of LAP at credit. So 210 x (Rs 78,000 / 30) = 210 x Rs 2,600 = Rs 5,46,000.

q: A railway servant on tour remains absent from his headquarters for 8 hours on a day, and the admissible rate of Daily Allowance for the station is Rs 750 per day. Daily Allowance for an absence of more than 6 hours but not exceeding 12 hours being admissible at 70 per cent of the rate, the amount admissible to him for that day will be:

options.B: Rs 525
options.C: Rs 750
options.D: Rs 375

e: Under the TA Rules, absence above 6 hours and up to 12 hours earns DA at 70 per cent of the full rate. So 70 per cent of Rs 750 = Rs 525.

q: A railway servant retires from an apex-level post and his pension, worked out at 50 per cent of his emoluments, comes to more than the ceiling prescribed under the 7th CPC dispensation. The maximum pension actually admissible to him is:

options.B: Rs 1,00,000 per month
options.C: Rs 1,25,000 per month
options.D: Rs 75,000 per month

e: Under the 7th CPC, maximum pension is 50 per cent of the highest pay of Rs 2,50,000. So the ceiling is Rs 1,25,000 per month.

q: The last pay drawn by a deceased railway servant was at the maximum of the pay structure, and the family pension of his family, worked out at the normal rate of 30 per cent of that pay, exceeds the ceiling prescribed under the 7th CPC dispensation. The maximum family pension admissible to his family at the normal rate is:

options.B: Rs 45,000 per month
options.C: Rs 1,25,000 per month
options.D: Rs 60,000 per month

e: Under the 7th CPC, maximum family pension at the normal rate is 30 per cent of the highest pay of Rs 2,50,000. So the ceiling is Rs 75,000 per month.

q: A railway servant retires on superannuation and opts to join the Retired Employees Liberalised Health Scheme (RELHS) for availing medical facilities after retirement. The one-time contribution payable by him for joining the Scheme is equal to:

options.A: Two months' basic pay last drawn by him
options.B: One month's basic pay last drawn by him
options.C: Six months' basic pay last drawn by him
options.D: A flat amount of Rs 10,000 in all cases

e: A retiree joining RELHS pays a one-time contribution equal to one month's basic pay last drawn, as prescribed for enrolment under the Scheme.

q: An order placing a railway servant under suspension, pending a departmental inquiry, is issued by the competent authority. The standard form in which such an order of suspension is issued under the Railway Servants (Discipline and Appeal) Rules is:

options.B: SF-11
options.C: SF-1
options.D: SF-7

e: Under the Railway Servants (Discipline and Appeal) Rules, the order of suspension is issued in Standard Form SF-1.

q: A railway servant who has completed only three years of service applies for study leave for a course of study connected with his duties. His application is liable to be rejected at the threshold because study leave is ordinarily admissible only to a railway servant who has completed a minimum service of:

options.B: 3 years
options.C: 10 years
options.D: 5 years

e: Study leave under the leave rules is ordinarily admissible only after completion of five years of service, so a servant with only three years is not eligible.

q: A subscriber to the General Provident Fund, who has completed 12 years of service and is not due to retire within the next twelve months, applies for a final, non-refundable withdrawal from the Fund for purchasing a house. In regard to his application, the correct position is that such a final withdrawal is ordinarily permissible only after he has completed:

options.B: 15 years of service
options.C: 12 years of service
options.D: 5 years of service

e: A final non-refundable GPF withdrawal for house purchase is ordinarily permissible only after 15 years of service, as per the GPF Rules; 12 years is not enough.

q: A railway servant has 300 days of Leave on Half Average Pay due to him and applies for commuted leave on medical certificate. In regard to the total amount of commuted leave that can be granted to him during his entire service, the correct position is that it shall not exceed:

options.A: One-fourth of the Leave on Half Average Pay due to him
options.B: The full amount of the Leave on Half Average Pay due to him
options.C: Half the amount of Leave on Half Average Pay due to him
options.D: 90 days in all, irrespective of the Leave on Half Average Pay due

e: Commuted leave is granted for double the amount of LHAP debited, and total commuted leave in entire service cannot exceed half the LHAP due. So the limit is half of the LHAP due.

q: A person appointed to railway service as a fresh recruit asks from when he can avail Leave Travel Concession every year in the initial period of his service. A fresh recruit is entitled to avail Leave Travel Concession every year during the first:

options.B: 4 years of service
options.C: 6 years of service
options.D: 10 years of service

e: Fresh recruits are allowed LTC every year, instead of in a block, during the first 8 years of service, as per the LTC instructions for new recruits.

q: While computing the Death-cum-Retirement Gratuity of a railway servant, an accounts clerk proposes to reckon as 'emoluments' his basic pay together with all the allowances drawn by him, including House Rent Allowance. The correct position is that the emoluments for this purpose are:

options.B: Basic pay plus House Rent Allowance only
options.C: Basic pay plus all allowances drawn by him
options.D: Basic pay plus the Dearness Allowance admissible on the relevant date

e: For DCRG, emoluments mean basic pay plus Dearness Allowance admissible on the relevant date. HRA and other allowances are not counted.

q: A railway servant who has opted for the Unified Pension Scheme finds that a deduction is being made from his pay every month towards his individual corpus under the Scheme. The contribution payable by him, as the employee, to his individual corpus is at the rate of:

options.A: 14% of Basic Pay plus Dearness Allowance
options.B: 10% of Basic Pay plus Dearness Allowance
options.C: 18.5% of Basic Pay plus Dearness Allowance
options.D: 8.33% of Basic Pay plus Dearness Allowance

e: Under UPS, the employee contributes 10 per cent of Basic Pay plus DA to the individual corpus; the matching Central Government contribution is separate.

q: A subscriber to the National Pension System retires on attaining the age of 60 years and wishes to withdraw the maximum permissible amount from his accumulated pension wealth as a lump sum, the balance being utilised for purchase of an annuity. The maximum lump sum withdrawal admissible to him is:

options.B: 25% of the accumulated pension wealth
options.C: 60% of the accumulated pension wealth
options.D: The entire accumulated pension wealth in all cases

e: On normal exit at 60 under NPS, up to 60 per cent of the accumulated pension wealth may be withdrawn as lump sum, the balance being used for annuity.

q: The case of a Group 'C' railway servant for premature retirement in public interest, under the relevant retirement rules, is taken up for review in the normal course. Such a review is ordinarily undertaken on his attaining the age of 55 years or on completion of:

options.A: 30 years of qualifying service, whichever is earlier
options.B: 20 years of qualifying service, whichever is earlier
options.C: 25 years of qualifying service, whichever is later
options.D: 33 years of qualifying service, whichever is later

e: Premature retirement in public interest for Group C staff is reviewed on attaining 55 years of age or completing 30 years of qualifying service, whichever is earlier.

q: A railway servant drawing basic pay of Rs 64,000 per month is sent on deputation to another organisation at the same station. The Deputation (Duty) Allowance admissible to him, at 5 per cent of his basic pay for deputation within the same station, will be:

options.B: Rs 4,500 per month
options.C: Rs 1,600 per month
options.D: Rs 3,200 per month

e: Deputation (Duty) Allowance within the same station is 5 per cent of basic pay. So 5 per cent of Rs 64,000 = Rs 3,200 per month.

q: A railway servant who has opted for the Unified Pension Scheme retires on superannuation after completing 25 years of qualifying service. The average of the basic pay drawn by him during the last 12 months of his service is Rs 64,000 per month. The assured monthly payout admissible to him under the Scheme, at 50 per cent of that average basic pay, will be:

options.B: Rs 32,000 per month
options.C: Rs 38,400 per month
options.D: Rs 16,000 per month

e: UPS assured payout after 25 years of qualifying service is 50 per cent of average basic pay of the last 12 months. So 50 per cent of Rs 64,000 = Rs 32,000.

q: A railway servant enquires from which dates in a year the revised instalments of Dearness Allowance, announced on the basis of the movement of the price index, are ordinarily made effective. The instalments of Dearness Allowance are ordinarily made effective from:

options.A: 1st January and 1st July of each year
options.B: 1st April and 1st October of each year
options.C: 1st March and 1st September of each year
options.D: The date of issue of the orders in each case

e: Dearness Allowance instalments, based on the price index, are ordinarily effective from 1st January and 1st July of each year.

q: A doubt arises in an office as to the authority which maintains the leave account of a gazetted railway servant serving in that office. The leave account of a gazetted railway servant is maintained by:

options.A: The office in which he is himself working
options.B: The Personnel Branch of the Zonal Railway Headquarters
options.C: The Accounts Office
options.D: The Railway Board

e: The leave account of a gazetted railway servant is maintained by the Accounts Office, unlike that of non-gazetted staff which is kept with the service record in the office.

q: A railway servant dies in service leaving behind two widows and no other eligible member of his family. A dispute arises between the two widows as to the sharing of the family pension admissible on his death. In regard to that family pension, the correct position is that it is:

options.A: Paid only to the elder of the two widows
options.B: Paid only to the widow who was living with him at the time of his death
options.C: Paid to his children, and not to either of the widows
options.D: Divided equally between the two widows

e: Where a deceased servant leaves two widows, family pension is divided equally between them under the Railway Pension Rules, when both are eligible.

q: A railway servant under suspension claims his subsistence allowance for a month. Before the allowance for that month is paid to him, he is required to furnish a certificate to the effect that he:

options.A: Is residing at his headquarters during the period of suspension
options.B: Is not engaged in any other employment, business, profession or vocation during the period in question
options.C: Has surrendered his railway passes and Privilege Ticket Orders
options.D: Has not engaged a legal practitioner for his defence

e: Subsistence allowance during suspension is paid only on a certificate that the servant was not engaged in any other employment, business, profession or vocation during that period.

q: In a departmental inquiry, the charged railway servant contends that the charges against him must be established beyond reasonable doubt, exactly as in a criminal trial, before any penalty can be imposed on him. In regard to the standard of proof in such an inquiry, the correct position is that the standard is:

options.A: Preponderance of probability, that is, the balance of probabilities
options.B: Proof beyond reasonable doubt, as in a criminal trial
options.C: Mere suspicion based on the report of the vigilance organisation
options.D: Documentary proof alone, oral evidence being inadmissible in such an inquiry

e: Departmental inquiries are decided on preponderance of probability, not on proof beyond reasonable doubt as required in a criminal trial.

q: A person who was engaged as an apprentice on the Railways for two years is thereafter appointed to a regular railway post and later claims that the period of his apprenticeship should be counted towards his qualifying service for pension. In regard to that claim, the correct position is that the period of apprenticeship:

options.A: Counts in full as qualifying service
options.B: Counts to the extent of one-half as qualifying service
options.C: Counts as qualifying service only if the apprenticeship exceeded two years
options.D: Does not count as qualifying service, as an apprentice is not a railway servant

e: An apprentice is not a railway servant, so the period of apprenticeship does not count as qualifying service for pension.

q: An accounts clerk, while computing the lump sum commuted value of the pension of a retired railway servant, proposes to work it out by simply multiplying the monthly pension surrendered by the commutation factor. The correct method of computing the lump sum commuted value is to multiply:

options.A: The monthly pension surrendered, by the commutation factor alone
options.B: The annual pension surrendered, by 15
options.C: The amount of monthly pension commuted, by 12 and by the commutation value (factor) for the age on the next birthday
options.D: The full monthly pension, whether commuted or not, by 12 and by the commutation factor

e: Commuted value equals monthly pension commuted x 12 x the commutation factor for age on the next birthday. Using the monthly amount alone with the factor would understate it.

q: A railway servant is granted Leave Not Due on medical certificate, no Leave on Half Average Pay being at his credit. The Accounts Office has to work out the leave salary payable to him for that period. The leave salary payable during Leave Not Due is equal to:

options.A: The leave salary admissible during Leave on Average Pay
options.B: Nil, as Leave Not Due carries no leave salary
options.C: 75 per cent of the leave salary admissible during Leave on Average Pay
options.D: The leave salary admissible during Leave on Half Average Pay

e: Leave salary during Leave Not Due equals the leave salary admissible during Leave on Half Average Pay, as Leave Not Due is granted in advance against future LHAP.

q: A railway servant proceeds on Leave on Half Average Pay for attending to his private affairs. The leave salary payable to him during that leave is:

options.A: Half of the leave salary admissible during Leave on Average Pay
options.B: Equal to the leave salary admissible during Leave on Average Pay
options.C: One-fourth of the leave salary admissible during Leave on Average Pay
options.D: Nil, as leave on private affairs carries no leave salary

e: Leave salary on LHAP is half the leave salary admissible on LAP, as prescribed in the leave rules for half-pay leave.

q: A railway servant is hospitalised for an injury attributable to his duty and is granted Work Related Illness and Injury Leave (WRIIL) for the period of his hospitalisation. The leave salary payable to him for that period of hospitalisation is:

options.B: Full pay
options.C: The leave salary admissible on Leave on Half Average Pay
options.D: No leave salary, the period being treated as dies non

e: During WRIIL for hospitalisation due to a work-related injury or illness, full pay is admissible for the hospitalisation period under the leave rules.

q: In a direct recruitment exercise for Level-1 posts on the Railways, a reservation is provided in favour of Course Completed Act Apprentices. The percentage of the vacancies so reserved for such apprentices is:

options.B: 25 per cent
options.C: 30 per cent
options.D: 20 per cent

e: In direct recruitment to Level-1 posts, 20 per cent of vacancies are reserved for Course Completed Act Apprentices as per the prescribed quota.

q: A Group 'A' railway officer accepts, on the occasion of his daughter's marriage, a gift worth Rs 40,000 from a personal friend who has no official dealings with him. In regard to reporting the acceptance of this gift to the Government, the correct position is that a report is required because the value of the gift exceeds:
e: For a Group A officer, gifts above Rs 25,000 must be reported under the Conduct Rules. A gift of Rs 40,000 therefore requires a report, even from a personal friend.

q: A subscriber to the General Provident Fund, whose monthly subscription is being deducted from his pay, wishes to raise the amount of that subscription during a financial year as his pay has increased. The number of times he may so enhance the amount of his monthly subscription during the course of a financial year is:

options.B: Not more than three times
options.C: Any number of times
options.D: Not more than twice

e: A GPF subscriber may enhance the monthly subscription not more than twice during a financial year, as per the GPF Rules.

q: A railway servant covered under the National Pension System draws basic pay of Rs 62,000 per month and Dearness Allowance is admissible to him at 50 per cent. The monthly contribution payable by the Government to his Tier-I account will be:
e: Government NPS contribution is 14 per cent of basic pay plus DA. Pay plus DA is Rs 62,000 + Rs 31,000 = Rs 93,000, and 14 per cent of that is Rs 13,020.

q: A female railway servant applies for Child Care Leave in a single spell of 3 days to attend to her minor child. The leave sanctioning authority finds that the spell applied for cannot be sanctioned because Child Care Leave cannot be granted in a spell of less than:

options.B: 10 days
options.C: 15 days
options.D: 30 days

e: Child Care Leave cannot be granted in a spell of less than 5 days, so a single spell of 3 days is not admissible.

q: A railway servant is transferred in public interest from one post to another post at the same station, and he joins the new post after handing over charge at the same station. The joining time admissible to him in this case is:

options.B: Three days
options.C: Seven days
options.D: Ten days

e: On transfer at the same station in public interest, only one day's joining time is admissible, as no travel or shifting of residence is involved.

q: A subscriber to the General Provident Fund has already enhanced the amount of his monthly subscription twice during the current financial year. He now seeks to enhance it a third time in the same financial year. The correct position is that:

options.A: The third enhancement is admissible with the sanction of the Head of Office
options.B: The third enhancement is admissible if the total subscription does not exceed his emoluments
options.C: The enhancement is admissible only from the next financial year in any case
options.D: A further enhancement is not permissible, as the subscription can be enhanced not more than twice in the course of a financial year

e: GPF subscription can be enhanced not more than twice in a financial year. A third enhancement in the same year is therefore not permissible.

q: An applicant submits his application under the Right to Information Act, 2005 to the Assistant Public Information Officer of a railway office. The information sought is required to be furnished to him within:

options.A: 30 days of the receipt of the application
options.B: 35 days of the receipt of the application
options.C: 45 days of the receipt of the application
options.D: 60 days of the receipt of the application

e: An RTI application received by an Assistant PIO must be furnished within 35 days, that is, the normal 30 days plus 5 days allowed for transfer to the PIO.

q: In a railway workshop governed by the Factories Act, 1948, a worker has worked continuously for five hours. Before he is required to work further, he must be given an interval for rest of at least:

options.B: Fifteen minutes
options.C: Forty-five minutes
options.D: One hour

e: Under Section 52 of the Factories Act, 1948, after five hours of continuous work a worker must get a rest interval of at least thirty minutes before working further.

q: A railway pensioner commuted a portion of his pension at the time of his retirement in April 2011 and the commuted value was paid to him in that month. The commuted portion of his pension will be restored to him on completion of:

options.A: 10 years from the date of commutation
options.B: 12 years from the date of his retirement
options.C: 15 years from the date of commutation
options.D: It will never be restored during his lifetime

e: The commuted portion of pension is restored after 15 years from the date of commutation, as per the commutation rules.

q: A subscriber under the Unified Pension Scheme dies after his retirement while receiving the assured payout. The family payout admissible to his legally wedded spouse will be:

options.A: 50 per cent of the payout admissible to the subscriber
options.B: 30 per cent of the payout admissible to the subscriber
options.C: 100 per cent of the payout admissible to the subscriber
options.D: 60 per cent of the payout admissible to the subscriber immediately before his death

e: On death of a UPS subscriber after retirement, the family payout to the legally wedded spouse is 60 per cent of the payout admissible to the subscriber immediately before death.

q: A railway servant is under suspension and disciplinary proceedings are also pending against him when the Departmental Promotion Committee considers his case for promotion. In accordance with the prescribed procedure, the recommendations of the Committee in his case are:

options.A: Acted upon immediately, as suspension is not a penalty
options.B: Kept in a sealed cover, to be acted upon after the conclusion of the proceedings against him
options.C: Recorded as an adverse recommendation against him
options.D: Deferred permanently and he is never considered again

e: When suspension and disciplinary proceedings are pending, DPC recommendations are kept in a sealed cover and acted upon only after conclusion of the proceedings.

q: A railway servant retires on superannuation with 150 days of Leave on Average Pay at his credit. His basic pay at retirement is Rs 72,000 per month and Dearness Allowance is admissible at 50 per cent. The cash equivalent of leave salary payable to him is:
e: Pay plus DA is Rs 72,000 + Rs 36,000 = Rs 1,08,000. Cash equivalent is 150 x (Rs 1,08,000 / 30) = 150 x Rs 3,600 = Rs 5,40,000.

q: A railway servant drawing basic pay of Rs 48,000 per month applies for House Building Advance for construction of a house, the estimated cost of construction being Rs 90 lakh. The maximum amount of advance admissible to him will be:
e: HBA is limited to 139 times monthly basic pay, subject to cost and ceiling limits. So 139 x Rs 48,000 = Rs 66,72,000, which is below the house cost.

q: A railway servant retires on superannuation after completing full qualifying service. His average emoluments are Rs 84,000 per month. The amount of his monthly pension will be:
e: Pension on superannuation is 50 per cent of average emoluments for full qualifying service. So 50 per cent of Rs 84,000 = Rs 42,000 per month.

q: The last basic pay drawn by a deceased railway servant was Rs 1,30,000 per month. The family pension payable to his family at the normal rate will be:

options.B: Rs 39,000 per month
options.C: Rs 26,000 per month
options.D: Rs 52,000 per month

e: Family pension at the normal rate is 30 per cent of last basic pay. So 30 per cent of Rs 1,30,000 = Rs 39,000 per month.

q: A railway servant retires on superannuation after rendering 32 years of qualifying service. His emoluments at the time of retirement are Rs 75,000 per month. The retirement gratuity admissible to him will be:
e: Retirement gratuity is one-fourth of emoluments per six-monthly period. For 32 years, that is 64 periods, giving 16 months x Rs 75,000 = Rs 12,00,000.

q: A railway pensioner's monthly pension is Rs 36,000. He commutes 40 per cent of his pension. Taking the commutation value for his age on the next birthday as 8.194 for each rupee of annual pension commuted, the lump sum commuted value payable to him will be:
e: Monthly pension commuted is 40 per cent of Rs 36,000 = Rs 14,400. Lump sum is Rs 14,400 x 12 x 8.194 = Rs 14,15,923.

q: A railway servant dies while in service after completing 7 years of qualifying service. His emoluments at the time of death are Rs 55,000 per month. The death gratuity payable to his family is:
e: Death gratuity for 5 to 20 years of qualifying service is 12 times emoluments. So for 7 years, 12 x Rs 55,000 = Rs 6,60,000.

q: A railway servant on tour is provided with both free boarding and free lodging by the Government for a day of his tour. The Daily Allowance admissible to him for that day is:

options.B: 25 per cent of the Daily Allowance
options.C: 50 per cent of the Daily Allowance
options.D: 70 per cent of the Daily Allowance

e: When both free boarding and free lodging are provided on tour, DA is restricted to 25 per cent of the admissible rate under the TA Rules.

q: The suspension of a railway servant is prolonged beyond three months and the competent authority finds that the prolongation is for reasons directly attributable to the railway servant himself. For the period beyond three months, his subsistence allowance may be:

options.A: Decreased by an amount not exceeding 50 per cent of the subsistence allowance admissible during the first three months
options.B: Increased by an amount not exceeding 50 per cent of the subsistence allowance admissible during the first three months
options.C: Converted into full pay and allowances for the remaining period
options.D: Withheld altogether till the conclusion of the proceedings

e: If suspension beyond three months is prolonged for reasons attributable to the servant, subsistence allowance may be decreased by up to 50 per cent of the first three months' allowance.

q: A member of the Central Government Employees Group Insurance Scheme retires from service. The amount payable to him on his retirement is:

options.A: Only the amount subscribed by him, without any interest
options.B: The insurance cover amount prescribed for his group
options.C: The amount at his credit in the Savings Fund of the Scheme, together with interest thereon
options.D: A fixed sum of Rs 30,000 in all cases

e: On retirement under CGEGIS, the member gets the amount at his credit in the Savings Fund of the Scheme together with interest, not merely his subscriptions.

q: A retiring railway servant wishes to join the Retired Employees Liberalised Health Scheme. The one-time contribution payable by him for joining the Scheme is equal to:

options.A: Two months' basic pay last drawn by him
options.B: Six months' basic pay last drawn by him
options.C: A flat amount of Rs 10,000
options.D: One month's basic pay last drawn by him

e: A retiree joining RELHS pays a one-time contribution equal to one month's basic pay last drawn, as prescribed for enrolment under the Scheme.

q: A railway pensioner does not avail the outdoor treatment facility under the health scheme and is accordingly entitled to Fixed Medical Allowance. Under the 7th CPC dispensation, the allowance admissible to him is:

options.B: Rs 1,000 per month
options.C: Rs 750 per month
options.D: Rs 2,000 per month

e: Pensioners not availing outdoor treatment are entitled to Fixed Medical Allowance of Rs 1,000 per month under the 7th CPC dispensation.

q: A post on a zonal Railway has remained continuously vacant for a period of more than five years and no action has been taken to fill it. In accordance with the instructions on creation and continuation of posts, such a post is:

options.B: Transferred to the Vacancy Bank of the Railway
options.C: Downgraded to the next lower level
options.D: Converted into a work-charged post

e: A post lying continuously vacant for more than five years with no action to fill it is deemed to have been abolished under the instructions on posts.

q: A worker has been engaged as project casual labour on a railway construction project and has been rendering continuous service since his engagement. The stage at which he becomes entitled to the grant of temporary status is on completion of continuous service of:

options.B: 240 days
options.C: 180 days
options.D: 365 days

e: Project casual labour becomes entitled to temporary status on completion of 180 days of continuous service on a project.

q: Certain persons have been engaged on the open line as substitutes in place of regular employees who are absent on leave. Such substitutes attain temporary status on completion of:

options.B: 240 days of continuous service
options.C: One year of continuous service
options.D: 120 days of continuous service

e: Substitutes engaged on the open line in place of absent regular employees attain temporary status on completion of 120 days of continuous service.

q: A railway servant tenders technical resignation from his post to take up another appointment under the Government with proper permission. He retains his lien on the post held by him in the parent cadre for a period of:

options.B: Two years
options.C: Three years
options.D: Five years

e: On technical resignation with proper permission to take up another Government appointment, lien on the parent post is retained for two years.

q: A railway servant discovers an error in the date of birth recorded in his service records and requests its alteration, showing that the error is a bona fide clerical error. Such a request can be entertained only if it is made within:

options.A: Five years of his entering service
options.B: Two years of his entering service
options.C: One year of his entering service
options.D: Ten years of his entering service

e: Alteration of date of birth for a bona fide clerical error can be entertained only if the request is made within five years of entering service.

q: A railway servant transferred in public interest has been permitted to retain the railway quarter at his old station for the initial period of two months on payment of normal licence fee. Retention of the quarter beyond that period may be permitted:

options.A: For a further period of six months on payment of normal licence fee
options.B: For a further period of two months on payment of normal licence fee
options.C: For a further period of two months on payment of double the licence fee
options.D: Only with the personal sanction of the Railway Board

e: After the initial two months on normal licence fee, a quarter on transfer may be retained for a further two months on payment of double the licence fee.

q: A railway servant proceeds on leave immediately after joining a new station and claims House Rent Allowance for the period of his leave. Subject to the prescribed conditions being fulfilled, House Rent Allowance continues to be admissible to him during the leave for a period not exceeding:

options.B: 120 days
options.C: 365 days
options.D: 180 days

e: Subject to conditions, HRA continues during leave for a period not exceeding 180 days, as per the HRA rules for staff on leave.

q: A railway servant is sanctioned leave preparatory to retirement. In regard to the period of such leave, the correct position is that it:

options.A: May extend up to six months beyond the date of his retirement
options.B: Cannot extend beyond the date on which he is due to retire from service
options.C: Is admissible only in the form of Leave on Average Pay
options.D: Is debited to the leave account of the succeeding year

e: Leave preparatory to retirement cannot extend beyond the date on which the servant is due to retire from service.

q: A railway servant remains absent from duty even after the expiry of the leave sanctioned to him, without obtaining any extension. In regard to the period of such overstayal, the correct position is that:

options.A: He is not entitled to any leave salary for that period, and the period may be treated as Extra Ordinary Leave
options.B: He is entitled to leave salary at the rate admissible on Leave on Average Pay
options.C: The period is automatically treated as a period spent on duty
options.D: The Accounts Office grants leave for that period on its own authority

e: For overstayal after expiry of sanctioned leave without extension, no leave salary is entitled and the period may be treated as Extra Ordinary Leave.

q: A railway servant on leave is recalled to duty compulsorily before the expiry of the leave sanctioned to him and he travels to join duty in compliance with the recall order. For the journey so undertaken by him, he is entitled to:

options.A: Double pay for the unexpired portion of his leave
options.B: A fresh spell of leave equal to the unexpired portion
options.C: Travelling allowance for the journey undertaken to join duty on recall
options.D: No facility of any kind

e: A servant recalled compulsorily from leave to duty is entitled to travelling allowance for the journey undertaken to join duty on recall.

q: Before proceeding on study leave for pursuing a course of study, a railway servant to whom such leave is granted is required to:

options.A: Deposit the entire leave salary drawn by him as security
options.B: Surrender his lien on the post held by him
options.C: Resign from service and seek reappointment on return
options.D: Execute a bond undertaking to serve the Railways for the specified period after his return from the study leave

e: Before study leave, the servant must execute a bond undertaking to serve the Railways for the specified period after return from study leave.

q: A question arises in an office as to the authority which maintains the leave account of a gazetted railway servant serving in that office. The leave account of a gazetted railway servant is maintained by:

options.A: The office in which he is himself working
options.B: The Accounts Office
options.C: The Personnel Branch of the Zonal Railway Headquarters
options.D: The Railway Board

e: The leave account of a gazetted railway servant is maintained by the Accounts Office, unlike that of non-gazetted staff which is kept in the office.

q: Departmental proceedings are pending against a railway servant on the date of his retirement and a provisional pension is sanctioned to him pending their conclusion. The provisional pension so sanctioned is equal to:

options.A: The maximum pension which would have been admissible to him on the basis of the qualifying service rendered up to the date of retirement
options.B: 50 per cent of the pension which would have been admissible to him
options.C: 75 per cent of the pension which would have been admissible to him
options.D: The minimum pension prescribed under the rules

e: Provisional pension pending departmental proceedings equals the maximum pension admissible on the qualifying service rendered up to the date of retirement.

q: A deceased railway servant has left behind two widows and no nomination for family pension subsists in favour of either of them alone. The family pension admissible in this case is:

options.A: Paid only to the elder of the two widows
options.B: Paid only to the widow who was living with him at the time of his death
options.C: Divided equally between the two widows
options.D: Paid to his children, and not to either widow

e: Where a deceased servant leaves two widows and no nomination subsists for one alone, family pension is divided equally between the two widows.

q: A candidate joins railway service on 15th March, 2005. In regard to the pension scheme applicable to him, the correct position is that:

options.A: He is covered under the Old Pension Scheme
options.B: He may opt either for the Old Pension Scheme or for the National Pension System
options.C: He is covered under the Old Pension Scheme, as he joined before 2016
options.D: He is covered under the National Pension System, which applies to railway servants who joined service on or after 1st January, 2004

e: NPS applies to railway servants who joined service on or after 1st January, 2004, so a servant joining on 15th March, 2005 is covered under NPS.

q: The pension payable to a railway pensioner works out to an amount involving a fraction of a rupee. In accordance with the pension rules, the amount of pension is rounded off:

options.B: To the next higher rupee
options.C: To the next lower rupee
options.D: It is paid in exact paise, without any rounding off

e: Pension involving a fraction of a rupee is rounded off to the next higher rupee under the pension rules.

q: A railway servant dies in the course of duty and ex-gratia lump sum compensation is found admissible to his family. In regard to this compensation, the correct position is that it is:

options.A: Payable in addition to family pension, death gratuity and other pensionary benefits
options.B: Adjusted against the death gratuity payable to the family
options.C: Admissible only where no family pension is payable
options.D: Payable in lieu of family pension

e: Ex-gratia lump sum compensation for death in the course of duty is payable in addition to family pension, death gratuity and other pensionary benefits.

q: A railway servant is compulsorily retired from service as a measure of penalty. The pension and gratuity admissible to him in such a case are at a rate:

options.A: Equal to one-half of the compensation pension in all cases
options.B: Equal to the full compensation pension in all cases
options.C: Not less than two-thirds and not more than the full amount of the pension or gratuity which would have been admissible to him had he retired on a compensation pension
options.D: Not admissible to him in any case

e: On compulsory retirement as a penalty, pension and gratuity are at not less than two-thirds and not more than the full compensation pension that would have been admissible.

q: A railway servant is promoted from a lower post to a higher post in the normal course. He is ordinarily placed on probation in the higher post for a period of:

options.B: Two years
options.C: Three years
options.D: One year

e: On promotion in the normal course, a railway servant is ordinarily placed on probation in the higher post for one year.

q: The services of a temporary railway servant are proposed to be terminated by the Railway Administration otherwise than as a measure of penalty. Such termination can be effected by giving him a notice of:

options.B: One calendar month, or pay in lieu thereof
options.C: Fifteen days in all cases
options.D: Six months in all cases

e: Services of a temporary railway servant, otherwise than as penalty, can be terminated by one calendar month's notice or pay in lieu thereof.

q: An order is issued placing a railway servant under suspension pending disciplinary proceedings against him. The order of suspension is issued in Standard Form:

options.B: SF-5
options.C: SF-7
options.D: SF-11

e: Under the Railway Servants (Discipline and Appeal) Rules, the order of suspension is issued in Standard Form SF-1.

q: A citizen files an application seeking information from a railway office under the Right to Information Act, 2005. The fee prescribed for making such an application is:

options.B: Rs 25
options.C: Rs 10
options.D: Rs 100

e: The fee prescribed for an RTI application under the RTI Act, 2005 is Rs 10.

q: A railway servant enters into a transaction in movable property in his own name. He is required to report the transaction to the prescribed authority where the value of the transaction exceeds:

options.B: Six months' basic pay
options.C: One year's basic pay
options.D: Two months' basic pay

e: A transaction in movable property must be reported under the Conduct Rules where its value exceeds two months' basic pay of the railway servant.

q: A gateman whose employment has been classified as 'Essentially Intermittent' under the Hours of Employment Regulations claims the weekly period of rest admissible to his classification. The minimum period of rest to which he is entitled in a week is:

options.A: 30 consecutive hours including one full night
options.B: 24 consecutive hours including one full night
options.C: 36 consecutive hours including one full night
options.D: 48 consecutive hours

e: A worker classified as Essentially Intermittent under HOER is entitled to a minimum weekly rest of 24 consecutive hours including one full night.

q: A railway servant is transferred in public interest and has to move his household effects to the new station. The pass issued to him for conveying his personal effects and luggage by train in connection with the transfer is known as a:

options.B: Kit Pass
options.C: Settlement Pass
options.D: Residential Card Pass

e: The pass issued on transfer for conveying personal effects and luggage by train is known as a Kit Pass.

q: A railway servant resides at a station away from his headquarters and commutes daily to his place of duty. The pass issued to him to travel between the station of his residence and the station of his duty is a:

options.B: Duty Card Pass
options.C: Residential Card Pass
options.D: Privilege Pass

e: A servant residing away from headquarters and commuting daily to duty is issued a Residential Card Pass between residence and duty stations.

q: The daughter of a railway servant is studying at an outstation school and has to travel home during vacations. The pass issued for her journey between the station of the school and the headquarters or residence of the railway servant is a:

options.B: Kit Pass
options.C: Metal Token Pass
options.D: Complimentary Pass

e: A School Pass is issued for the daughter's journey between the outstation school and the headquarters or residence of the railway servant during vacations.

q: A railway servant whose duties require him to travel frequently within a specified jurisdiction is issued a pass so that he can travel on duty without obtaining a separate pass for each journey. Such a pass is called a:

options.B: Residential Card Pass
options.C: Widow Pass
options.D: Duty Card Pass

e: A Duty Card Pass is issued to a servant who must travel frequently on duty within a jurisdiction, without a separate pass for each journey.

q: Metal token passes on the Railways, which serve as a standing authority for duty travel, are issued to:

options.B: Group 'A' and Group 'B' gazetted railway officers
options.C: Only railway servants in Level-1
options.D: Only the Chairman and Members of the Railway Board

e: Metal token passes, as a standing authority for duty travel, are issued to Group A and Group B gazetted railway officers.

q: A privilege pass issued to a railway servant remains valid for undertaking the journey for a period of:

options.A: One month from the date of issue
options.B: Two months from the date of issue
options.C: Three months from the date of issue
options.D: Five months from the date of issue

e: A privilege pass remains valid for undertaking the journey for five months from the date of issue, as per the Pass Rules.

q: A Group 'C' railway servant retires after rendering 26 years of service and claims post-retirement complimentary passes. The number of sets of such passes admissible to him in a year is:

options.B: Two sets
options.C: Three sets
options.D: Six sets

e: A retired Group C servant with 20 years or more of service, here 26 years, is entitled to two sets of post-retirement complimentary passes per year.

q: The widow of a deceased retired railway servant claims the complimentary passes admissible to her after his death. Such passes are issued to her at the rate of:

options.A: The same number of sets as was admissible to the deceased railway servant
options.B: One set only during the whole period of her widowhood
options.C: Half the number of sets of post-retirement complimentary passes admissible to the deceased railway servant, subject to a minimum of one set in alternate years
options.D: Two sets in every calendar year, irrespective of the entitlement of the deceased

e: A widow gets half the number of sets of post-retirement complimentary passes admissible to the deceased servant, subject to a minimum of one set in alternate years.

q: A railway servant is placed in the Aye-Two (A-2) medical category for the purpose of his duties. The standard of distant vision prescribed for this category is:

options.B: 6/6, 6/6 without glasses
options.C: 6/12, 6/12 with or without glasses
options.D: 6/18, 6/18 with or without glasses

e: For medical category A-2, the distant vision standard is 6/9, 6/9 with or without glasses, as prescribed in the medical classification.

q: A railway servant is placed in the Bee-One (B-1) medical category. The standard of distant vision prescribed for this category is:

options.B: 6/12, 6/12 without glasses
options.C: 6/9, 6/12 with or without glasses
options.D: 6/18, 6/18 with or without glasses

e: For medical category B-1, the distant vision standard is 6/9, 6/12 with or without glasses, as prescribed in the medical classification.

q: For the purpose of the pay rules, 'average pay' of a railway servant means:

options.A: The average monthly pay earned by him during the twelve complete months immediately preceding the month in which the event requiring its calculation occurs
options.B: The pay drawn by him in the last month of his service
options.C: The average monthly pay earned by him during the last ten months of his service
options.D: The average monthly pay earned by him during the last three years of his service

e: Average pay means the average monthly pay earned during the twelve complete months immediately preceding the month in which the event requiring its calculation occurs.

q: Under the Fundamental Rules, a 'compensatory allowance' admissible to a railway servant means:

options.A: A fee paid to him for work of an occasional or intermittent character
options.B: The pay drawn by him in an officiating appointment
options.C: An allowance granted to him for holding additional charge of another post
options.D: An allowance granted to meet personal expenditure necessitated by the special circumstances in which duty is performed

e: A compensatory allowance is an allowance granted to meet personal expenditure necessitated by the special circumstances in which duty is performed, under the Fundamental Rules.

q: An officer is appointed to a post on the condition that he may hold it only for a limited term, even though the post itself is permanent in nature. Such a post is classified under the Fundamental Rules as a:

options.A: A permanent post which an individual railway servant may not ordinarily hold for more than a limited period
options.B: A post held by a railway servant during his period of probation
options.C: A temporary post sanctioned for a work of short duration
options.D: A post from which a railway servant can be removed at any time without notice

e: A tenure post is a permanent post which an individual railway servant may not ordinarily hold for more than a limited period, under the Fundamental Rules.

q: For establishment purposes, the sanctioned strength of a service, or of a distinct part of a service treated as a separate unit, is referred to in the Fundamental Rules as its:

options.A: The seniority list of a service
options.B: The strength of a service, or a part of a service, sanctioned as a separate unit
options.C: The total number of employees working in an office at a given time
options.D: A group of officers recruited to a service in the same year

e: Cadre means the sanctioned strength of a service, or of a distinct part of a service treated and sanctioned as a separate unit, under the Fundamental Rules.

q: A railway servant retires from service after rendering 8 years of qualifying service and is accordingly not entitled to pension. His emoluments at the time of retirement are Rs 38,000 per month. The service gratuity payable to him, at half a month's emoluments for each completed six-monthly period of qualifying service, will be:
e: Service gratuity is half a month's emoluments per six-monthly period. For 8 years, that is 16 periods, giving 8 months x Rs 38,000 = Rs 3,04,000.

q: A railway servant covered under the National Pension System draws basic pay of Rs 38,000 per month and Dearness Allowance at 50 per cent of basic pay. The monthly contribution payable by the railway servant himself to his Tier-I account, at 10 per cent of basic pay plus Dearness Allowance, will be:
e: Employee NPS contribution is 10 per cent of basic pay plus DA. Pay plus DA is Rs 38,000 + Rs 19,000 = Rs 57,000, and 10 per cent is Rs 5,700.

q: The pay of a gazetted railway servant in an office is drawn by the establishment on the basis of an authority issued for the purpose showing the pay and allowances admissible to him. That authority, the pay slip, is issued by:

options.B: The Railway Recruitment Board
options.C: The recognised officers' association of the Railway
options.D: The gazetted railway servant himself, by self-declaration

e: The pay slip, showing pay and allowances admissible to a gazetted servant and authorising drawal of his pay, is issued by the Accounts Office.

q: A claim for arrears of pay and allowances of a railway servant is not preferred within one year of the date on which it became due. Before such a claim can be paid, it is required to be subjected to:

options.A: A vigilance inquiry by the Vigilance Department
options.B: Pre-audit by the Accounts Office, in accordance with the rules for investigation of arrear claims
options.C: The approval of the Railway Board in every case
options.D: An inquiry by the Central Administrative Tribunal

e: An arrear claim not preferred within one year of becoming due must be subjected to pre-audit by the Accounts Office under the rules for investigation of arrear claims.

q: The pay for a month has already been disbursed, and arrears for an earlier period thereafter become payable to a clerk because of a retrospective pay fixation order. These arrears are claimed by the establishment through:

options.A: A supplementary pay bill prepared for the purpose
options.B: The travelling allowance bill of the railway servant
options.C: The contingent bill of the office
options.D: A fresh appointment order issued by the competent authority

e: Arrears becoming payable after the month's pay has been disbursed, due to retrospective fixation, are claimed through a supplementary pay bill.

q: The statement attached to a supplementary pay bill, setting out in respect of each railway servant the amount of pay and allowances due to him, the amount already drawn by him and the net amount now claimed, is known as the:

options.B: Increment certificate
options.C: Last Pay Certificate
options.D: Due-drawn statement

e: The statement attached to a supplementary pay bill showing amount due, amount already drawn and net amount claimed for each servant is the due-drawn statement.

q: In addition to the Head of Office verifying and attesting the entries in a Service Book every year, the rules also require that:

options.A: It is sent to the Accounts Office every year for safe custody
options.B: It is shown to the railway servant concerned every year and his signature obtained in it in token of his having seen it
options.C: It is shown to the railway servant only at the time of his retirement
options.D: It is rewritten afresh every five years by the office

e: Besides annual verification by the Head of Office, the Service Book must be shown to the servant every year and his signature obtained in token of having seen it.

q: The original Service Book of a railway servant is lost in his office. In regard to the record of his service, the correct position is that:

options.A: A fresh service record is started from the date of loss, ignoring the earlier service
options.B: The railway servant is treated as a fresh entrant for all purposes
options.C: A duplicate Service Book may be prepared by the Head of Office on the basis of the available records, the past entries being verified and reconstructed as far as possible
options.D: No duplicate Service Book can be prepared under any circumstances

e: If the original Service Book is lost, a duplicate may be prepared by the Head of Office from available records, with past entries verified and reconstructed as far as possible.

q: A doubt arises in a divisional office about who keeps the leave account of a non-gazetted clerk serving in that office. The account is kept:

options.A: By the Accounts Office which checks his pay bills
options.B: By the pension section of the zonal railway headquarters
options.C: In the prescribed form, along with his Service Book, by the office in which he is serving
options.D: By the office of the General Manager of the zonal railway

e: The leave account of a non-gazetted servant is kept in the prescribed form along with his Service Book by the office in which he is serving.

q: The leave account of a railway servant is lost and is not available in his office. In such a case, the leave account is reconstructed:

options.A: On the basis of available collateral records, such as pay bills, absentee statements and the entries in his Service Book
options.B: By crediting him with 300 days of Leave on Average Pay in all cases
options.C: Only from the date of the loss, ignoring the leave availed of by him earlier
options.D: Solely on the basis of a declaration made by the railway servant himself

e: A lost leave account is reconstructed from available collateral records such as pay bills, absentee statements and entries in the Service Book.

q: A railway servant applies, after availing a spell of leave, for its conversion into another kind of leave. Such conversion by the leave sanctioning authority is permissible provided that:

options.A: The railway servant refunds the whole of the leave salary already drawn by him
options.B: The other kind of leave was due and admissible to him at the time the leave originally granted was availed of
options.C: The Railway Board sanctions the conversion in every case
options.D: The conversion is sought only within one year before his retirement

e: Conversion of leave into another kind is permissible only if that other kind of leave was due and admissible when the leave originally granted was availed of.
